title: India Women Crush South Africa 6-1 in Hockey World Cup Opener
excerpt: Salima Tete's side scored in all three quarters before South Africa managed a consolation, as India delivered a dominant Pool D performance in Amstelveen.
body:
• India crushed South Africa 6-1 in their FIH Women's Hockey World Cup Pool D match at the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen on August 18.
  • Salima Tete's side scored in each of the first three quarters, building a commanding 6-0 lead before South Africa pulled one back in the fourth.
  • India enter the tournament on the back of winning the FIH Nations Cup in New Zealand without losing a single match.
  • The team's final group match is against England on August 20, with qualification to the second round at stake.

India's women's hockey team delivered a dominant performance at the FIH Women's Hockey World Cup, routing South Africa 6-1 in their Pool D encounter at the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, on Tuesday.

Captain Salima Tete's squad was clinical from the start, scoring in each of the first three quarters to build an insurmountable 6-0 lead before South Africa managed a consolation goal in the final period.

Quarter-by-Quarter Dominance

India set the tone early, taking a 1-0 lead in the first quarter. The side, coached by Sjoerd Marijne, then doubled down in the second period with two more goals to go into the half leading 3-0. The third quarter brought India's most prolific spell — three goals in 15 minutes that extinguished any hope of a South African comeback and made the scoreline 6-0.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2089736666231750731

South Africa, who had already lost 4-0 to England in their opening match, avoided a shutout with a fourth-quarter goal but were thoroughly outclassed across the 60 minutes.

India's attacking firepower was on full display. Dragflicker Deepika Sehrawat, who scored six goals in five matches at the recent Nations Cup, and forwards Navneet Kaur and Lalremsiami were central to India's relentless pressure in the circle.

Marijne's Second Coming

The victory is a vindication of the decision to bring back Sjoerd Marijne as chief coach in February 2026. The Dutchman previously coached India's women's team to a historic fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 — the team's best-ever Olympic result.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=MyFOe_FH5Ss

"We have chosen a well-balanced group of players who are ready for the big challenges we will face this summer. The team has worked hard in the lead-up to the tournament and we are confident in this group's abilities."

— Sjoerd Marijne, India women's hockey chief coach

Under Marijne's renewed charge, India won the FIH Nations Cup in New Zealand in June without losing a match, beating the hosts 2-0 in the final. That title also secured India's return to the top-tier FIH Pro League for the 2026-27 season.

Pool D Outlook

India are placed in Pool D alongside England, China, and South Africa. The 16-team tournament, co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands, runs from August 15-30. In a format change from previous editions, the standard quarterfinal knockout stage has been replaced by a second round involving eight teams, who play two additional matches before progressing to the semifinals.

India's final group match is against England on August 20 at the same venue — a rematch of the World Cup qualifier final earlier this year, which England won. A result against the higher-ranked English side would put India in a strong position to advance.

A Squad Built for the Moment

Tete, the 24-year-old midfielder and Arjuna Award winner, leads a squad that blends experience with emerging talent. Veteran goalkeeper Savita anchors the defense, while young midfielder Sakshi Rana and forward Beauty Dungdung have impressed in recent international outings.

The squad entered the World Cup with momentum and confidence. "This time, Hockey World Cup will be ours," Tete declared before the tournament opener. Tuesday's demolition of South Africa suggests India may have the firepower to back up their captain's ambition.
